first_impression.reaction: OK, the first paragraph actually answers me: spring in Europe, autumn in New Zealand, wet season in the tropics. The last bit of that sentence trips over itself though, I had to read it twice on the train. The takeaways give me the ten places straight away, which is what I came for.

journey.quote: It is early spring in Europe, autumn in New Zealand, and across much of the tropics the closing weeks of the wet or cyclone season, which is still that season.
journey.reaction: Good answer up top, but 'which is still that season' reads like a typo. Just say it's still wet season.

journey.quote: The ten are the Greek islands, Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast, the French Riviera and Portugal in Europe's early spring, and New Zealand, Mauritius, the Seychelles, Bali and Fiji in the southern autumn and late summer.
journey.reaction: This is the answer. Ten places, split by hemisphere, in one line. If I only read this I've got what I searched for.

journey.quote: Fiji, Mauritius and the Seychelles are inside the cyclone or monsoon season Smartraveller describes for March, so a covered ceremony option and a buffer day are part of the booking.
journey.reaction: Useful and honest. Citing a government travel site makes me trust it more than the usual 'tropical paradise' stuff.

journey.quote: Each station uses its own period and rain-day definition, so read every figure on its own and choose on trade-offs, not on numbers set side by side.
journey.reaction: This is a footnote, not a takeaway. On my phone it takes up a whole bullet and tells me nothing about where to go.

journey.section: How we chose these ten March destinations
journey.quote: The figures come from city or island stations, which can differ from a villa nearby.
journey.reaction: Fair caveat but I'm scrolling past this. Two methodology paragraphs before the first destination is a lot.

journey.quote: give a March mean daily minimum of 3.8°C, a mean daily maximum of 14.3°C and 65.0 mm of rain over 6.7 rain days.
journey.reaction: Real numbers with a source and years. 3.8 at night, so it's jacket weather. That's the kind of specific I want.

journey.quote: Milan is a city station, not a lakeside one, and the page does not define its rain day.
journey.reaction: Honest, but these station disclaimers repeat in every entry. By the third one I'm skimming them.

journey.quote: On 25 and 26 March a deep subtropical low brought heavy rain and flooding, with states of emergency and road closures from Northland to the Bay of Plenty.
journey.reaction: Dated and specific, it feels current. Answers my 'is this still true in 2026?' question.

journey.section: Wedding destinations in March at a glance
journey.quote: | Fiji | Wet season, cyclone season | Cyclones and flooding |
journey.reaction: The table is exactly what I want on a phone, but it's way down the page. The intro mentions it but there's no way to jump to it.

journey.quote: Where is warm for a wedding in March?
journey.reaction: Good FAQ, it's the second thing I'd have Googled. Short answers, no waffle.

unanswered_questions: How much does a March wedding in any of these places cost? The page doesn't give any idea of budget.
Is March cheaper or less busy than peak months anywhere on this list? The page doesn't say.
Which of the European options is the mildest in the evening? I'd have to compare the numbers myself, and the page tells me not to.
What does Wedded Concierge actually do and what does it cost? The page says the fee is agreed in writing but not what it is or what it covers.

turn_offs_found.quote: Each station uses its own period and rain-day definition, so read every figure on its own and choose on trade-offs, not on numbers set side by side.
turn_offs_found.why: A method caveat sitting in Key Takeaways, the one bit I actually read. It pushes the useful stuff down.

turn_offs_found.quote: The ten wedding destinations in March below are unranked and grouped by what the month means in each place, with a table at a glance after the entries.
turn_offs_found.why: Tells me there's a summary table but makes me scroll through ten entries to reach it. No jump link.

would_share_with: My fiancé, the Key Takeaways and table only

cta_reaction.quote: Torn between a cool European spring and a warm, wet island? Talk it through with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-march&utm_content=primary).
cta_reaction.why: The question is exactly where I am, so it lands. But I don't know this brand and I came for a quick answer, not to talk to anyone yet. I'd bookmark the page before I'd click.

Link the intro's mention of the table straight to the at-a-glance table so phone readers can jump there.
